_handoff.scopeNote: Official-source pass for a new BESCOM electricity connection in Bengaluru. Public BESCOM pages, FAQ, eligibility guidance, and BESCOM-hosted KERC conditions were inspected only. No account, applicant identity, temporary ID, document, payment, or application was entered. Thresholds, charges, field validation, and final supply remain case-specific and are not inferred beyond the published pages.

meta.title: Bengaluru BESCOM new electricity connection official-source pass
meta.disclaimer: Research handoff, not official advice. BESCOM's FAQ, home page, and eligibility page use slightly different fast-track load wording; confirm the applicable current category and demand before relying on a timeline or amount.

sources.title: BESCOM Frequently Asked Questions
sources.notes: Current public FAQ describes Janasnehi Vidyuth Sevegalu and normal new-connection routes, visible steps, documents, payment boundaries, and 1912 help.

sources.title: BESCOM New Connection public form
sources.notes: Public form exposes application-type, temporary-account-ID, personal-details, supply-address, correspondence-address, location/miscellaneous, and document-upload stages. No value was entered.

sources.title: BESCOM Eligibility for New Connection
sources.notes: Publishes Janasnehi scope/exclusions and required payment, agreement, test-report, ID/address verification, and solar-water-heater undertaking conditions.

sources.title: BESCOM official home
sources.notes: Current home page advertises Janasnehi fast-track service and a Bengaluru EODB route with displayed timelines; these are subject to category and infrastructure conditions.

sources.title: Conditions of Supply of Electricity with I and II Amendments
sources.notes: Officially hosted consolidated conditions. The document contains historic/dated material; use as regulatory context and verify later KERC amendments before treating a clause or time frame as current.

claims.text: BESCOM's public FAQ says a customer can select New Connection under Janasnehi Vidyuth Sevegalu without customer-portal login, accept the disclaimer, select single or multiple connection, optionally provide a temporary account ID, enter personal/address/location/load details, upload documents, submit, and view a charge breakdown/demand letter.
claims.notes: No application or payment was started.

claims.text: BESCOM's FAQ distinguishes a normal New Connection route under Other Services for LT, HT/EHT, and MC/MSB, with application type, personal/address, miscellaneous/load, contractor where applicable, confirmation, and charge-breakdown steps.
claims.notes: The FAQ describes a route; property/network eligibility and case outcome remain Unknown.

claims.text: BESCOM's eligibility page says Janasnehi fast-track applies to LT-1 domestic and LT-3 commercial services up to 18 kW excluding 18 kW, including new and tapping connections, and excludes line-extension/modification cases, certain tall/large or unauthorised premises, HT category, and incomplete wiring/meter-board/service cable.
claims.notes: Eligibility page wording is current public guidance, not a property-specific decision.

claims.text: BESCOM's FAQ and home page describe the Janasnehi fast-track load ceiling as up to 17.5 kW, while the eligibility page says up to 18 kW excluding 18 kW; the applicable threshold should therefore be confirmed for the chosen route.
claims.notes: This records a wording difference, not a resolved legal threshold.

claims.text: BESCOM's public FAQ lists document classes including registered sale/gift/partition deed, khata, latest tax receipt, registered lease, occupancy certificate, solar-water-heater compliance, identity/address and other conditional technical or undertaking documents; the eligibility page requires prescribed documents to be verified with originals and lists power-supply agreement and contractor completion/test report conditions.
claims.notes: The list is not a universal checklist; requiredness depends on category, premises, load, and route.

claims.text: BESCOM's home page displays power supply within 24 hours after requisite-fee payment for qualifying domestic LT-1 and commercial LT-3 consumers up to the fast-track load limit where no line extension is needed; it also displays a Bengaluru EODB new-connection target of 7 days without RoW and 15 days with RoW for stated LT/HT load bands.
claims.notes: Displayed service targets are conditional labels, not a guarantee for an unclassified property or a proof that payment starts the clock in every case.

claims.text: BESCOM's FAQ says that for normal new connection, only the application fee can be paid online and remaining additional charges are paid by visiting the SDO office; the actual amount and applicable route are not known without a case.
claims.notes: Do not generalize this payment statement to every JVS/EODB category.

claims.text: The BESCOM-hosted KERC conditions provide regulatory context for supply applications and time frames, but the hosted consolidated copy is dated and cannot by itself establish the complete current workflow, fee schedule, or outcome.

roadblocks.title: Fast-track threshold wording differs
roadblocks.symptom: FAQ/home page say 17.5 kW while eligibility says 18 kW excluding 18 kW.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Different page versions or inclusive/exclusive wording.
roadblocks.recovery: Confirm the applicable current route and load ceiling with BESCOM before relying on fast-track eligibility.

roadblocks.title: Network and premise eligibility is case-specific
roadblocks.symptom: Public pages cannot decide line extension, RoW, building height/plinth, occupancy-certificate, wiring, arrears, or tariff conditions for a property.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Requires applicant, load, premises, and field verification.
roadblocks.recovery: Use the public form only with the applicant's own information and retain the generated request/demand reference; no data was submitted in this pass.

roadblocks.title: Hosted conditions are not a full current compilation
roadblocks.symptom: The BESCOM-hosted KERC conditions contain dated material while current pages advertise newer routes and targets.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Portal and regulatory documents have different update cycles.
roadblocks.recovery: Treat the PDF as context and verify the current KERC/BESCOM rule before asserting a binding deadline or charge.
